profile.headline: Software Engineer II at AT&T/DIRECTV
profile.summary:
As an artist and programmer, I’ve always been a creative and logical thinker. In my artistic side, I would draw comic books every day as a kid and show it to my friends and family. In high school, I fell in love with filmmaking and I would create music videos  and short films and upload them on social media. 

In my logical side, I love solving math problems and thinking logically. Math has always made the most sense to me from all of my subjects. I always feel a sense of accomplishment whenever I solve a problem. Seeing math applied to so many real-world situations is so intriguing to me.

When I discovered programming towards the end of senior year, I decided to pursue computer science because of its versatility in almost every field and industry. Programming would allow me to explore and discover so many ways of expressing my love for art and problem solving. I could apply mathematical concepts such as algebra, calculus, geometry, matrices and graphs as well as my visual aesthetics to create innovative and profound works to influence and shape the world.  

Right now, I am interested in pursuing software, app, and web development as well as computer graphics because they involve design and technical artistry. Being able to combine my two strengths and passions in the real world is definitely what I want in my career.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.locationName: El Segundo, California, United States · Remote
positions.description:
- DIRECTV STREAM video streaming service - unified codebase among multiple platforms (ios/android mobile/tablet, TVOS, FireTV, Web, Samsung, Chromecast): work on resolving incidents/production bugs, monitoring/improving player KPIs, and utilizing new features (React Native/Typescript/Objective C)
• Daily sync-ups and documenting reports on app and video performance: investigating spikes and abnormalities using dashboards and adding resiliency to codebases; integrated libraries for reporting metrics
• Continuous delivery through CICD pipelines, automating code quality/security checks, and deployment
• Collaboration across back-end dev teams and product owners to improve architecture; mentoring other members
• Maintaining npm and internal packages that are shared among clients, working with DevOps team to improve workflow and add automations to development life cycle; managed deployments in Kubernetes

projects.title: ONLINE E-COMMERCE SITE: PIXEL STORE
projects.description:
•developed with a team of 3 using Java servlets (Model-View-Controller approach: EL, JSTL, and Java Beans)
•implemented session for shopping cart and checkout for unique browser
•allowed user to add, edit, and remove items through inventory manager (can upload image for each item)
•implemented search function in main page which only displayed certain items based on keyword(s)
•implemented item details page which shows description, price, and quantity available for each item
•deployed on CS3 server and FTP (.java, .jsp, .css, .jpeg, .png)
•managed mySQL database of all the items of the store including transaction history through phpMyAdmin
•designed web layout through CSS and Bootstrap framework

projects.title: Color Matching Game (JavaFX)
projects.description:
A color matching game made with JavaFX by Chelle Cruz.

RULES 
Choose 6 colors from the grid of many colors! 225 colors to be exact! Your goal is to make the grid one color by matching with different colors around you. You will start off in the upper left box in the beginning of the game. Continue to match colors around you in order to win. You have 30 tries. Have fun!

IMPLEMENTATION
Implemented game logic through pickColors() method that allows player to customize and choose 6 colors from grid of random colors (15 x 15)
Designed a recursive algorithm called matchNext() that matches color squares on the grid for every move

learning new programming languages through workshops, working on group projects such as Magic Mirror (implemented user recognition from digital camera through Windows API mediaCapture and Microsoft’s Cognitive Services Face API using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for client-side)
